2609.15129.title: Medical Knowledge Simplification for Patients in the Era of LLMs: A Case Study on Diabetes
2609.15129.paper_summary: Complex medical information is often difficult for patients to understand, making effective medical knowledge simplification essential for improving patient comprehension, informed decision-making, and health outcomes. Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) provide a promising approach for simplifying complex medical information into patient-friendly language; however, their effectiveness in real-world patient education remains insufficiently explored through human evaluation. To investigate their practical effectiveness, this paper presents a case study on diabetes knowledge simplification through the implementation and evaluation of MediClear, an LLM-based medical knowledge simplification system enhanced with Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG). Public diabetes-related articles from Diabetes Australia, WHO, American Diabetes Association (ADA), NIDDK, and AIHW are indexed in the RAG knowledge base to retrieve clinically grounded information, which is then simplified by the LLM into accessible patient explanations. We evaluate the generated responses using standard readability metrics, including the Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level (FKGL), and conduct a human study involving 10 participants. Results show that MediClear consistently reduces the reading level of generated responses to the recommended patient literacy range while achieving high user satisfaction and willingness for future use. This case study demonstrates the potential of LLMs to improve the accessibility of medical knowledge for patient education.
2609.15129.paper_summary_zh: 複雜的醫療資訊對患者而言往往難以理解，因此有效的醫療知識簡化對於改善患者理解、知情決策和健康結果至關重要。最近大型語言模型（LLMs）的進展為將複雜醫療資訊簡化為患者友好的語言提供了一種有前景的方法；然而，它們在現實世界中的患者教育中的有效性仍然缺乏通過人類評估的充分探索。為了調查它們的實際有效性，本文呈現了一個關於糖尿病知識簡化的案例研究，通過實施和評估MediClear，一個基於LLM的醫療知識簡化系統，並增強了檢索增強生成（RAG）。來自糖尿病澳大利亞、世界衛生組織、美國糖尿病協會（ADA）、NIDDK和AIHW的公共糖尿病相關文章被編入RAG知識庫，以檢索臨床基礎的資訊，然後由LLM簡化為可供患者理解的解釋。我們使用標準可讀性指標來評估生成的回應，包括Flesch-Kincaid年級水平（FKGL），並進行了一項涉及10名參與者的人類研究。結果顯示，MediClear始終將生成回應的閱讀水平降低到建議的患者識字範圍內，同時實現了高用戶滿意度和未來使用的意願。這個案例研究展示了LLMs在改善醫療知識可及性以促進患者教育方面的潛力。
